name: Ajax 1994/95
scopeNote: Ajax 1994/95: Dutch Supercup (1994-08-21) to the last Eredivisie match (1995-05-27), including the Champions League won on 1995-05-24. Tactical evidence rests on one match analysis (Spielverlagerung on the final v Milan, 3-3-4 structure in possession); no source found uses a single style label, and Van Gaal's stated view was not found. Dates are exact, from Wikipedia season and Champions League pages.
openQuestions: The academy count (13 of 18) is unverified: the FourFourTwo page was empty.
Formation labels disagree in unread secondary sources (4-3-3, 3-3-1-3, 4-2-3-1); only the 3-3-4 structure in possession (final) is verified.
Pressing, marking and Van Gaal's stated view need a dedicated source (Ajax archive match briefings, Coaches' Voice).

sources.title: Amsterdam's last night of European glory (Glenn Billingham)
sources.evidence: "the average age of Ajax's starting 11 was a staggering 22" … "Adding the experienced defenders, that number only increases to 24." "18-year-old Patrick Kluivert." Experienced core: Rijkaard (back from Milan in 1993), Blind.

sources.title: Search summary citing FourFourTwo
sources.evidence: Summary only: 13 of the 18 players in the final squad came through the academy; average age 23. The page came back empty.

sources.title: 1995 Champions League final: AFC Ajax – AC Milan 1:0 (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: "Ajax were giving Milan trouble simply by using a 3-3-4 structure while in possession." "This occupied the back line very well while controlling the center of the pitch in both midfield and defense." Single match (the final).

sources.title: 1995 Champions League final: AFC Ajax – AC Milan 1:0 (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: "they relied mostly on the speed of their passing in simple combinations"; "Ajax lacked dynamics in offense and retained the ball for a long time." Single match.

sources.title: 1995 Champions League final: AFC Ajax – AC Milan 1:0 (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Ajax controlled possession and "retained the ball for a long time" against Milan. Single match.

sources.title: 1995 Champions League final: AFC Ajax – AC Milan 1:0 (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Ajax lost the ball often after vertical passes ("they won the ball quite often after an Ajax vertical pass"); "AC Milan lacked any real counterpressing during this game." Single match.

sources.title: 1995 Champions League final: AFC Ajax – AC Milan 1:0 (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: "Another bright moment for Ajax was when Finidi dropped deeper on the wing and Reiziger played the ball into him." Single match.

sources.title: 1994–95 AFC Ajax season (Wikipedia)
sources.evidence: First competitive match 1994-08-21 (Supercup, 3-0 Feyenoord); last Eredivisie match 1995-05-27 (3-1 Twente). Manager Louis van Gaal, captain Danny Blind; Kluivert top scorer 18 goals; Bogarde and Reiziger signed. No tactical text on the page (first 100k characters read).

sources.title: 1994–95 UEFA Champions League (Wikipedia)
sources.evidence: Final "24 May 1995", Ernst-Happel-Stadion, Vienna, Ajax 1-0 Milan, Kluivert 85th minute. Knockouts: Hajduk Split 3-0 agg, Bayern Munich 5-2 agg.

confidence.reason: Tactical evidence is one tier B match analysis (the final) plus tier C Wikipedia dates and one tier B squad-age source; pressing, marking and stated view unverified.
